assistant_text:
Without the link from Price rise to monthly recurring revenue, the recorded evidence doesn't establish that the tested conclusions hold or change.

What I tested: the same model and inputs, recomputed with only this link removed. The two Runs are separately sampled (unpaired). It compares these two model versions; it doesn't say which version of the model is right.

What holds:
- Keep pricing as is's expected result is the same without the link, and stays below your target.
- Launch starter tier's expected result is about the same without the link (the difference is within sampling noise), and stays below your target.

What remains uncertain:
- At least one run withheld this claim.
- The difference is within sampling noise.
- The figures can be compared, but no supported conclusion boundary is available.
- Driver rankings and other diagnostic scores aren't compared between the two versions, because they shift with how the model is scaled.
- All of Olumi's other estimates were kept as they are; this is one alternative, not the only one.
- This test isn't saved. You can run it again while the model stays as it is.

Next step: resolve the missing or unqualified evidence before drawing a conclusion about how Price rise affects monthly recurring revenue.

No single option can be put forward yet, because the options came out too close together on this run to tell apart; tell me what matters most to you between them.
